# Part 7 — Episode anatomy

Finally, the descriptive natural history. An **episode** is a maximal run of days on which a
city's PBB-Score is at or above 2σ, allowing gaps of up to two days to be bridged (a
single quiet Sunday inside an otherwise continuous panic should not split one episode into
two).

```{r ep-setup}
EP_DIR <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "episode_anatomy")
EXTREME_THRESHOLD <- 3.0
GAP_TOLERANCE     <- 2

identify_runs <- function(x, gap_tolerance = 0) {
  x <- as.integer(x)
  if (gap_tolerance > 0) {
    rl <- rle(x)
    bridge <- rl$values == 0 & rl$lengths <= gap_tolerance &
      c(FALSE, head(rl$values, -1) == 1) & c(tail(rl$values, -1) == 1, FALSE)
    rl$values[bridge] <- 1
    x <- inverse.rle(rl)
  }
  rl <- rle(x)
  run_id <- rep(NA_integer_, length(x))
  if (any(rl$values == 1)) {
    starts <- cumsum(c(1, head(rl$lengths, -1)))
    ends   <- starts + rl$lengths - 1
    k <- 0
    for (j in seq_along(rl$values)) if (rl$values[j] == 1) {
      k <- k + 1; run_id[starts[j]:ends[j]] <- k
    }
  }
  run_id
}
```

```{r ep-identify}
ep_df <- read.csv2(PANEL_CSV, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
ep_df$date <- as.Date(ep_df$date)
ep_df <- ep_df %>% filter(!is.na(API)) %>% arrange(city, date) %>%
  mutate(panic_flag   = as.integer(API >= PANIC_THRESHOLD),
         extreme_flag = as.integer(API >= EXTREME_THRESHOLD))

episodes <- ep_df %>%
  group_by(city) %>%
  mutate(episode_id = identify_runs(panic_flag, GAP_TOLERANCE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(episode_id)) %>%
  group_by(city, episode_id) %>%
  summarise(start_date    = min(date),
            end_date      = max(date),
            duration_days = as.integer(end_date - start_date) + 1L,
            n_panic_days  = sum(panic_flag, na.rm = TRUE),
            peak_PBB      = max(API, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_PBB      = mean(API[panic_flag == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
            is_extreme    = as.integer(any(extreme_flag == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(year = year(start_date))

# An episode is labelled by a crisis type if its interval OVERLAPS any window of that type.
# The regime calendar (with the documented v9 omissions) is reused from Part 6.
overlaps <- function(s, e, cal) {
  Reduce(`|`, Map(function(ws, we) s <= we & e >= ws, cal$start, cal$end))
}

episodes <- episodes %>%
  mutate(is_pandemic = overlaps(start_date, end_date, by_type$pandemic),
         is_climate  = overlaps(start_date, end_date, by_type$climate),
         is_geopol   = overlaps(start_date, end_date, by_type$geopolitical),
         # Prioritised label: acute (climate/geopolitical) overrides chronic (pandemic)
         crisis_type = case_when(is_climate  ~ "Climate",
                                 is_geopol   ~ "Geopolitical",
                                 is_pandemic ~ "Pandemic",
                                 TRUE        ~ "Unattributed"))

write.csv(episodes, file.path(EP_DIR, "episode_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("Episodes identified: %d across %d municipalities\n",
            nrow(episodes), n_distinct(episodes$city)))
```

The prioritised label needs justification. The pandemic windows span years, so almost every
climate or geopolitical episode in 2020–2022 *also* falls inside a pandemic window. Attributing
those to "pandemic" would make the pandemic look like the cause of everything. We therefore let
the **acute, short-window** hazard take precedence over the **chronic, long-window** one.

```{r ep-summary}
ep_summary <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Total episodes", "Municipalities with >= 1 episode",
             "Mean duration (days)", "Median duration (days)", "Max duration (days)",
             "Mean peak PBB-Score", "Episodes containing an extreme (>= 3σ) day",
             "Episodes per city-year"),
  Value = c(nrow(episodes),
            n_distinct(episodes$city),
            round(mean(episodes$duration_days), 2),
            median(episodes$duration_days),
            max(episodes$duration_days),
            round(mean(episodes$peak_PBB), 2),
            sum(episodes$is_extreme),
            round(nrow(episodes) / (n_distinct(episodes$city) * n_distinct(episodes$year)), 2))
)
knitr::kable(ep_summary, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Episode anatomy — headline statistics")

ct <- episodes %>% count(crisis_type) %>%
  mutate(share = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n / sum(n))) %>% arrange(desc(n))
knitr::kable(ct, col.names = c("Crisis context", "Episodes", "Share"),
             caption = "Episodes by crisis attribution (prioritised labelling)")
```

## Sensitivity to the gap tolerance

The two-day bridge is a judgement call, so it should be shown to be inconsequential:

```{r ep-gap-sensitivity}
gap_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0, 1, 2, 5), function(g) {
  n <- ep_df %>% group_by(city) %>%
    mutate(eid = identify_runs(panic_flag, g)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(eid)) %>% distinct(city, eid) %>% nrow()
  data.frame(`Gap tolerance (days)` = g, Episodes = n, check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(gap_tab, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Episode count as a function of the gap-bridging tolerance")
```

## Figures

```{r ep-figs, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}
crisis_colors <- c(Pandemic = "#E65F2B", Climate = "#2A9D8F",
                   Geopolitical = "#0099B8", Unattributed = "#8D99AE")

# Pin the crisis_type factor so every panel uses the same four levels / colours,
# whether or not a given panel actually contains all of them.
episodes <- episodes %>%
  mutate(crisis_type = factor(crisis_type,
                              levels = c("Pandemic", "Climate", "Geopolitical", "Unattributed")))

# (a) episodes per year, stacked by crisis type
p_year <- episodes %>% count(year, crisis_type, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(year), n, fill = crisis_type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = crisis_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Number of episodes", fill = NULL, tag = "(a)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# (b) episodes per city, sorted, stacked by crisis type
city_order   <- episodes %>% count(city) %>% arrange(n) %>% pull(city)
p_city <- episodes %>% count(city, crisis_type, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(city = factor(city, levels = city_order)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(city, n, fill = crisis_type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = crisis_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of episodes", fill = NULL, tag = "(b)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "none", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# (c) duration distribution — a STACKED histogram coloured by crisis type
#     (not a single-colour histogram)
p_dur <- ggplot(episodes, aes(duration_days, fill = crisis_type)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = crisis_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30)) +
  labs(x = "Episode duration (days)", y = "Number of episodes",
       fill = NULL, tag = "(c)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# (d) peak-intensity distribution — a histogram of peak PBB coloured by crisis type,
#     with the 3σ extreme line (this is a distribution, NOT a duration-vs-peak scatter)
p_sev <- ggplot(episodes, aes(peak_PBB, fill = crisis_type)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = EXTREME_THRESHOLD, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = EXTREME_THRESHOLD, y = Inf, label = " Extreme (3σ)",
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = crisis_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Peak PBB-Score", y = "Number of episodes", fill = NULL, tag = "(d)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# Composition-level legend via plot_annotation (ggplot2 4.x-safe; no `&` on patchwork)
ep_panel <- ((p_year + p_city) / (p_dur + p_sev)) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(theme = theme(legend.position = "bottom",
                                legend.text   = element_text(size = 10),
                                legend.margin = margin(t = -4)))
ep_panel
ggsave(file.path(EP_DIR, "episode_anatomy_panel.png"), ep_panel,
       width = 11, height = 8, dpi = 300)
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "PDFs", "Figure_3.pdf"), ep_panel, width = 11, height = 8)
```

## Data availability

The SEF/SC *Nota Fiscal* transaction data underlying `total_sales_value_daily` are provided
by the Santa Catarina State Treasury. All other inputs are public: IBGE/SIDRA (IPCA food
sub-index, population), Google Trends, INMET (meteorology), Meta Movement Distribution Maps
(mobility, 2022 onward), and Globo/G1 headline counts.
